description: The embedded REPORTS extension pack -- the opt-in, isolated report bundle: the four report namespaces (`source`/`period`/`audience`/`cadence`) plus ONE general `{match, apply}` rule-set matching `type:report`. Carries NO generic vocabulary (no required fields, no description caps, no file_class rules, no exempt entries) -- it is meant to be layered ON TOP of a base pack that supplies the `type` namespace (e.g. `default@1.0.0`), never used standalone. `type` is the rule-set's match namespace and is owned by the base pack; the merge resolves that cross-pack reference against the fully-merged profile regardless of layer order. A repo that does not need report semantics simply omits this pack from its `navigator.toml` extensions.

description_caps.source: This pack adds no description-cap classes -- classification is `default@1.0.0`'s job.

file_class.note: Matches `default@1.0.0`'s own `default` value so layering never triggers a spurious override warning; this pack adds no file_class rules of its own -- classification is `default@1.0.0`'s job.

namespaces.name: source
namespaces.source: The report's data-source axis -- required on a `type:report` file (rule-set require_namespaces), forbidden elsewhere (forbidden_unless_matched).

namespaces.name: period
namespaces.source: The report's covered calendar window -- required on a `type:report` file, forbidden elsewhere. `type: date_interval` -- a downstream range-eligibility consumer (facetquery) treats this facet's value as a closed date range and matches on OVERLAP against a query window, not equality; the rule-set value_format also calendar-checks it.

namespaces.name: audience
namespaces.source: The report's intended consumer -- allowed only on a `type:report` file (forbidden_unless_matched), optional even there.

namespaces.name: cadence
namespaces.source: The report's refresh frequency -- allowed only on a `type:report` file, optional; defaults to on-demand when unspecified.

rule_sets.notes: Both directions together define the report semantics: on a `type:report` file `source`/`period` are required (`cadence`/`audience` stay optional) and `period` is format- and calendar-checked; on any other file all four report namespaces are forbidden. `forbidden_unless_matched` lists the four namespaces in pack-declared order so the emitted misuse-violation order is stable. The `value_formats` regex uses explicit ASCII `[0-9]` rather than `\d`: the Rust validator compiles it with the `regex` crate, whose `\d` matches any Unicode decimal digit by default, so `[0-9]` (ASCII-only) rejects e.g. Arabic-Indic digits an un-flagged `\d` would accept. The value_format `message` (not core) carries the format-specific wording, so a differently-formatted pack reuses this mechanism with its own message.
rule_sets.source: The report axis expressed as one instance of the general core@2.0.0 rule-set construct; there is no report-named special case.

exempt.source: This pack adds no exemptions -- the generated/exempt taxonomy is `default@1.0.0`'s job.
